'''Alfonzo McKinnie''' (born September 17, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Busan KCC Egis]] of the [[Basketball Champions League Asia]]. He played college basketball for [[Eastern Illinois University]] and [[University of Wisconsin–Green Bay]].

==Early life==
McKinnie grew up on [[West Side, Chicago|Chicago's West Side]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=McKinnie making most of 'dream come true' with Bulls|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/bulls/bulls-alfonzo-mckinnie-making-most-biggest-dream-come-true|access-date=2021-12-26|website=RSN|language=en}}</ref> Growing up just in [[East Garfield Park, Chicago|East Garfield Park]] only about 15 minutes from the [[United Center]], he describes himself as an enthusiastic supporter of the [[Chicago Bulls]] in youth.<ref name=":0" /> McKinnie played his first two years of high school basketball at Chicago's [[Curie Metropolitan High School]].<ref name="EiuBio" /> He played his final high school season as a starter at [[Marshall Metropolitan High School]], during which he earned All-Red West Conference honors averaging 11.2 points and 8.5 rebounds per game.<ref name="EiuBio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.eiupanthers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1755|title=Alfonzo McKinnie Bio|work=eiupanthers.com|access-date=July 10, 2017}}</ref>

==College career==
McKinnie was not a big scorer and lightly recruited during his one year at Marshall HS. He got a chance to play at Eastern Illinois. As a sophomore he averaged 10.2 points and 7.0 rebounds per game.<ref name="RealGM">{{Cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Alfonzo-McKinnie/Summary/22478#NCAA|title=NCAA Season Stats – Per Game|work=RealGM.com|access-date=July 10, 2017}}</ref> After his second year, he transferred to Wisconsin-Green Bay, where he tore his [[Meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]] at the end of his redshirt season. Later, he tore his meniscus again and had it removed.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://windycity.gleague.nba.com/news/chicago-native-alfonzo-mckinnie-shines-windy-city-bulls/|title=Chicago Native Alfonzo McKinnie Shines For Windy City Bulls|work=NBA.com|date=December 27, 2016|access-date=July 10, 2017}}</ref> He finished his college career averaging 7.1 points and 5.1 rebounds in 96 games.<ref name="RealGM"/>

==Professional career==
===East Side Pirates (2015–2016)===
After going undrafted in the [[2015 NBA draft]], McKinnie started his career with the East Side Pirates<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Luxembourg/news/415780/East-Side-adds-McKinnie-to-their-roster|title=East Side adds McKinnie to their roster|date=August 6, 2015|work=eurobasket.com|access-date=August 6, 2015}}</ref> in Luxembourg's semi-professional second division, where he became the go-to scorer, averaging 26 points per game.<ref name="RidUpside">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ridiculousupside.com/2017/3/28/15062194/alfonzo-mckinnie-windy-city-bulls-nba-dleague-nbadl|title=How Alfonzo McKinnie Became A D-League All-Star|work=ridiculousupside.com|date=March 28, 2017|access-date=July 10, 2017|archive-date=July 18, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180718001321/https://www.ridiculousupside.com/2017/3/28/15062194/alfonzo-mckinnie-windy-city-bulls-nba-dleague-nbadl|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Rayos de Hermosillo (2016)===
On May 21, 2016, he signed with the Mexican team [[Rayos de Hermosillo]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/Luxembourg/news/447377/Hermosillo-inks-Alfonzo-McKinnie,-ex-East-Side|title=Hermosillo inks Alfonzo McKinnie, ex East Side|work=eurobasket.com|date=May 21, 2016|access-date=July 10, 2017}}</ref> An old friend, former [[North Dakota Fighting Hawks men's basketball|North Dakota]] forward Emmanuel Little, suggested he join the [[CIBACOPA]]. McKinnie became a strong player on the squad. He helped lead the Rayos to the regular-season title and the final series before falling four games to two against the Náuticos de Mazatlán.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gomez |first1=Eric |title=Americans call the Mexican basketball league home |url=http://www.espn.com/blog/onenacion/post/_/id/8169/american-players-call-the-mexican-basketball-league-home |access-date=August 22, 2018 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=December 7, 2017}}</ref>

===Windy City Bulls (2016–2017)===
In September 2016, McKinnie paid 175 dollars for a tryout with the [[Windy City Bulls]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref name="RidUpside"/> On October 30, 2016, he made Bulls’ G-League roster.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://windycity.gleague.nba.com/news/windy-city-bulls-select-four-players-2016-d-league-draft-complete-training-camp-roster/|title=Windy City Bulls Select Four Players in 2016 D-League Draft to Complete Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2016|access-date=July 10, 2017}}</ref> He played well for the Bulls in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Letourneau |first1=Connor |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/warriors/article/Alfonzo-McKinnie-takes-unique-journey-to-13306407.php|title=Alfonzo McKinnie takes 'unique journey' to roster spot with Warriors|work=San Francisco Chronicle |date=October 14, 2018|access-date=October 30, 2018}}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2017–2018)===
On July 9, 2017, McKinnie signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/raptors-sign-malcolm-miller-alfonzo-mckinnie|title=Raptors Sign Malcolm Miller and Alfonzo McKinnie|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2017|access-date=July 10, 2017}}</ref> He made his NBA debut on October 19, 2017, playing in a single minute in their 117–100 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]]. During his rookie season, he received multiple assignments to [[Raptors 905]], Toronto's [[NBA G League]] affiliate.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Raptors-905/41/Transaction_History/2018|title=2017–2018 Raptors 905 Transactions History|work=RealGM.com|access-date=April 15, 2018}}</ref> On July 17, 2018, the Raptors waived McKinnie.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/raptors-waive-mckinnie|title=Raptors Waive Alfonzo McKinnie|work=NBA.com|date=July 17, 2018}}</ref>

===Golden State Warriors (2018–2019)===
McKinnie signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the [[2018–19 NBA season|2018–19 season]]. He ultimately earned a spot on the team's opening night roster.<ref>{{cite web|first=Connor|last=Letourneau|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/warriors/article/Alfonzo-McKinnie-takes-unique-journey-to-13306407.php|title=Alfonzo McKinnie takes 'unique journey' to roster spot with Warriors|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|date=October 14, 2018|access-date=October 17, 2018}}</ref> He recorded his career first [[double-double]] (19 points, 10 rebounds, both career highs) in 27 minutes off the bench on October 29 against the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://watch.nba.com/game/20181029/GSWCHI|title=GAME RECAP: Warriors 149, Bulls 124|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=October 29, 2018|access-date=October 29, 2018}}</ref> McKinnie averaged 4.7 points a game for the season while playing 72 games. The Warriors advanced to the [[2019 NBA Finals]], where they lost to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in six games. On October 18, 2019, the Warriors waived McKinnie.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-waive-mckinnie-cunningham-zeisloft-20191019|title=Warriors Waive McKinnie, Cunningham and Zeisloft|date=October 19, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 19, 2019}}</ref>

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2019–2020)===
On October 21, 2019, the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] claimed McKinnie off waivers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/alfonzo-mckinnie-claimed-191021|title=Cavaliers Claim Alfonzo McKinnie off Waivers|date=October 21, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 21, 2019}}</ref> On January 6, 2020, he was waived by the Cavaliers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/waive-mckinnie-cook-200106|title=Cavaliers Sign Levi Randolph; Waive McKinnie, Cook|date=January 6, 2020|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 6, 2020}}</ref> On January 9, the Cavaliers signed him to a 10-day contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/mckinnie-10-day-200109|title= Cavs Sign Alfonzo McKinnie To 10-Day Contract|date=January 9, 2020|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 9, 2020}}</ref> On January 23, McKinnie was re-signed to a second 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cavs Sign Alfonzo McKinnie To Second 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/mckinnie-10-day-200123 |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 23, 2020 |date=January 23, 2020}}</ref> On February 8, 2020, the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] announced that they had signed McKinnie to a multi-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/mckinnie-multi-year-contract-200208|title=Cavaliers Sign Alfonzo McKinnie to Multi-Year Contract|date=February 8, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 8, 2020}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2020–2021)===
On November 22, 2020, McKinnie, along with [[Jordan Bell]], was traded to the Lakers in exchange for [[JaVale McGee]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Lakers Acquire Jordan Bell and Alfonzo McKinnie|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-acquire-jordan-bell-and-alfonzo-mckinnie|website=NBA.com|date=November 22, 2020|access-date=November 23, 2020}}</ref> On August 4, 2021, he was waived by the Lakers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lakers Waive Alfonzo McKinnie|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-waive-alfonzo-mckinnie|website=NBA.com|date=August 4, 2021|access-date=August 4, 2021}}</ref>

===Mexico City Capitanes (2021)===
On October 25, 2021, McKinnie signed with the [[Mexico City Capitanes]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=CAPITANES|number=1452673812252659713|title=💎 • Una absoluta joya esta tarjeta. Un jugador con mucha experiencia a nivel @NBAMEX: 🃏 • ALFONZO MCKINNIE 🌎 • EEUU 🇺🇸 🏀 • SF Bienvenido a CAPITANES, @_Alvo_‼️ #AlfonzoEsCapitán 💙💛|user=CapitanesCDMX|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=October 31, 2021}}</ref> In 10 games, he averaged 24.1 points, 9.8 rebounds and 1.5 assists.<ref name="Bulls10D">{{cite web|title=BULLS SIGN ALFONZO MCKINNIE TO 10-DAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-alfonzo-mckinnie-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 10, 2021|access-date=December 11, 2021}}</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2021–2022)===
On December 10, 2021, McKinnie signed a 10-day contract with his hometown team, the [[Chicago Bulls]], due to numerous players on the team testing positive for COVID-19.<ref name="Bulls10D" /> On December 20, he signed a second 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Chicago Bulls|number=1473004030834233352|title=We have signed Alfonzo McKinnie to a second 10-day contract|user=chicagobulls|date=December 20, 2021|access-date=December 20, 2021}}</ref> McKinnie described the move to the Chicago Bulls as "the biggest dream coming true".<ref>{{cite web|first=K.C.|last=Johnson|work=NBCSports.com|title=McKinnie making most of 'dream come true' with Bulls|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/bulls/bulls-alfonzo-mckinnie-making-most-biggest-dream-come-true|date=December 21, 2021|access-date=April 5, 2022|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220118193932/https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/bulls/bulls-alfonzo-mckinnie-making-most-biggest-dream-come-true|archive-date=January 18, 2022}}</ref> On December 26, McKinnie was signed for the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-release-alize-johnson-sign-alfonzo-mckinnie|date=26 December 2021|title=BULLS RELEASE ALIZE JOHNSON, SIGN ALFONZO MCKINNIE|website=NBA.com|accessdate=26 December 2021}}</ref> On February 19, 2022, he was waived.<ref>{{Cite web|title=BULLS RELEASE MCKINNIE; SIGN THOMPSON|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/draft-bulls-sign-tristan-thompson|access-date=February 19, 2022|website=NBA}}</ref>

===Return to Mexico City (2022–2023)===
On November 4, 2022, McKinnie was named to the opening night roster for the [[Mexico City Capitanes]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Capitanes de Ciudad de México roster 2022-23|url=https://capitanes.gleague.nba.com/roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 4, 2022|access-date=November 4, 2022}}</ref>

===Dinamo Banco di Sardegna Sassari (2023–2024)===
On September 21, 2023, McKinnie signed with [[Dinamo Sassari|Dinamo Banco di Sardegna Sassari]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Mckinnie è un nuovo gigante|url=https://www.dinamobasket.com/it/blog/mckinnie-%C3%A8-un-nuovo-gigante|website=DinamoBasket.com|date=September 21, 2023|access-date=September 21, 2023|language=Italian}}</ref>

===Busan KCC Egis (2024)===
In June 2024, McKinnie joined to [[Busan KCC Egis]] for [[2024 Basketball Champions League Asia]].<ref>{{cite web |title=아시아 농구 챔피언스리그 대진 확정... '맥키니-탐슨 가세' KCC 한국 대표로 출격 | work=ROOKIE |url=https://www.rookie.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=98953 |access-date=29 September 2024 |date=3 June 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=KCC에 합류한 골든스테이트 출신 맥키니, KBL에 관심이 많았던 이유는? |url=https://www.basketkorea.com/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065576017637275 |publisher=바스켓코리아 |access-date=29 September 2024 |date=5 June 2024}}</ref>

On July 29, 2024, McKinnie signed with the [[Kobe Storks]] of the [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=アルフォンゾ・マッキニー選手 契約締結（新規）のお知らせ |url=https://www.storks.jp/news/detail/id=18278 |publisher=神戸ストークス |access-date=29 September 2024 |date=29 July 2024}}</ref> On August 23, 2024, his contract was terminated due to medical examination.<ref>{{cite web |title=アルフォンゾ・マッキニー選手 契約解除のお知らせ |url=https://www.storks.jp/news/detail/id=18303 |publisher=神戸ストークス |access-date=29 September 2024 |date=23 August 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He is the son of Elisa Bryant and Alfonzo McKinnie Sr.<ref name="EiuBio"/> In 2018, during his first stop in Chicago with the Warriors, he signed papers to buy his mother a house,  and introduced his parents at the Warriors team dinner after he helped Golden State blow out the Bulls.

He was previously engaged to Johanna Leia.
